name: Phaser drums: ping a phaser's all-pass filter bank with a very short impulse (a gate/trigger or just the attack of a sample), raise feedback/resonance until the bank rings like a tom, use more poles for complex liquid timbres, and sequence the sweep (centre frequency) and resonance per step to get tuned, accented percussion
goal: Turn any phaser into a resonant percussion voice. Delta vs phaser cluster (phaser pads, four-bar ramps, notch/comb movement, building a phaser from all-pass stages): here the phaser is the sound source, excited by impulses (filter pinging), not a modulation effect on a sustained pad.

source.title: Phaser Drums - How to turn a Phaser into a Drum Synthesizer

prerequisites: Any phaser with feedback/resonance and pole-count controls (hardware or plugin)
A trigger/gate source or a sampler that can play only a very short attack slice
A step sequencer or MIDI clip with automation/modulation lanes

inputs.name: impulse
inputs.description: Very short click/gate or the first few ms of a sample

outputs.name: phaser_percussion
outputs.description: Liquid tom/bell-like tuned percussion from a ringing all-pass bank

constraints: Start with phaser feedback low and output level down; high resonance can self-oscillate and jump in level, so keep a limiter on the track.
Per-step pitch values are fixed sequenced notes; no random sweep or wobble (Matt's preference).
Keep hits sparse, not rapid rolls or clicks; drums still enter early (~8 counts / ~12 s) if this is the main percussion.
Portable: any phaser with feedback and pole count; a trigger into an audio input on hardware equals a sampler playing a 1-5 ms attack slice in a DAW.

Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with Ableton, Reason, Bitwig, Soundtoys, FabFilter, Eventide or any vendor. Map product devices to generic modules (sampler, noise osc, filter, envelope, LFO, EQ, saturator, compressor, delay, reverb) in any DAW, hardware or Web Audio.
Steady pitch: no random pitch wobble or randomised notes; no rapid clicking textures (Matt's preference).

steps.action: Set the phaser's LFO depth/rate to minimum so it doesn't sweep on its own; keep only the output up.
Feed a very short impulse into the phaser: a gate/trigger pulse, or a sampler playing only the attack portion of any sample.
Raise feedback/resonance until the click rings with body.
steps.expect: Tom-like pitched ring after each hit

steps.action: Increase the pole/stage count (e.g. 4 to 8 to 12) for more complex, liquid timbres; try the phaser's alternative mode if it has one for a drummier tone.
Turn the sweep/centre frequency by hand to find the tuning range, then sequence it per step (automation or CV/mod lane) to play a melodic percussion line in key.
Sequence feedback/resonance per step too, so some hits ring longer as accents.
Optionally modulate the phaser's internal LFO rate/amount slowly for evolving timbre, then add reverb.

verification: With the impulse alone the sound is a click; with feedback up it rings at a pitch set by the sweep.
Changing sweep per step changes the hit pitch to the sequenced notes.
Peak level stays under the limiter ceiling at maximum resonance.
